summary: A custom X-band pulsed EPR spectrometer based on a 16-strip YBCO superconducting microstrip resonator achieves automated measurement of spin-labeled protein samples at sub-10 μM concentrations using 3.5 μL sample volumes with $\pm1$ degree phase stability. The system implements advanced DEER protocols (RELOAD, DEER-Stitch, CPMG echo train detection) to achieve 6× SNR improvement and enables unattended sequential measurement of five samples in a single cartridge with performance competitive to standard Q-band systems.
motivation: Superconducting resonators offer intrinsic per-spin sensitivity advantages over conventional EPR cavities, but their small mode volumes limit detection of biophysically relevant samples at physiologically relevant concentrations ($<10$ μM) in large sample volumes needed for structural biology applications.
method: A novel patterned 16-microstrip YBCO resonator (operating at $9.447$ GHz with $Q \approx 80$ and bandwidth $\sim125$ MHz) was designed to achieve superlinear scaling of sample volume with number of strips, yielding 2.4 μL homogeneous volume with $\bar{g} = 0.12$ Hz. An FPGA-based spectrometer with 1 ns pulse resolution, 500 MHz digitizer bandwidth, and digital IF generation enables stable acquisition and implementation of advanced pulse sequences (shaped Gaussian/adiabatic pulses, RELOAD, DEER-Stitch, CPMG echo trains) with automated calibration routines.
result: Distance measurements of spin-labeled T4-Lysozyme and YopO proteins achieved SNR of 128 for 90 μM T4L and SNR 25 for 25 μM YopO in 12.5 hours (comparable to Q-band round-robin benchmarks), with sub-10 μM capability demonstrated at 5 μM. Automated cartridge measurements of five biradical rulers with distances 2.85–7.52 nm completed in $<12$ hours with SNR 13–104, requiring approximately 120-fold improvement in per-spin sensitivity (factor of 15 from resonator design, factor of 8 from advanced methodologies).
